raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t like to toss money around. On my 5 mu, I’ll still do what has kept the family steady: most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, and a smaller piece in cotton so I’m not relying on one thing only. I only finished primary school, so I don’t count everything too finely. I look at what my own field did, and what the neighbors around me are doing. Wheat and maize are the backbone here, and with the well I can keep them safe if spring or summer rain is short. Cotton takes more watching and more hand work, so I won’t put too much land in it at my age.

For wheat-maize, I’ll keep about 3 mu in that rotation. Wheat I plant in early October, same as usual, with a local good seed or the one the seed dealer says everybody is using. I’ll put a base fertilizer before sowing, then one more topdress when the wheat starts standing up strong in spring. If the year is dry, I’ll irrigate around wintering, jointing, and maybe filling, but I won’t overdo it because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll rush to plant summer maize right away. That land can’t wait. I’ll use hybrid maize seed because saved maize seed is not reliable. For cotton, I’ll keep 2 mu. Cotton can bring cash if the price is decent, but it needs more hand labor and more spraying, so I only keep a small area. I’ll fertilize it a bit lighter than wheat-maize and irrigate only when I see it really needs water. That way I keep some cash in hand and don’t make the year too risky.
